trust_decision.summary: When a 3xx Location resolves to a different origin, the next hop must carry no Authorization/Cookie/Proxy-Authorization header and must not re-apply options.auth or options.digestAuth (nor the same credentials merged in from client defaultArgs); same-origin redirects keep everything. Decided in the redirect branch of HttpClient.#requestInternal, and re-decided on every hop of the redirect chain.

landing_point.why: This is the only place in the pinned tree that follows a redirect: it resolves Location against the current URL and recurses into #requestInternal with the caller's original `options`, so the next hop rebuilds the same credential headers from the same per-call options.

fix_sites.module_kind: core request implementation, redirect loop (#requestInternal), TS/CJS+ESM build
second implementation for the legacy 2.x/3.x branch, changed by commit 7c86c46 — this file does not exist at the pinned commit (4.9.0 tree ships only src/)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: defaultArgs is caller-supplied client configuration stored at construction (src/HttpClient.ts:191-193), and the redirect branch only ever receives the per-call options object, so a solver can argue the client-defaults merge is outside a report that shows only per-request headers/auth.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Same-origin redirects must keep Authorization/Cookie/Proxy-Authorization and keep working for options.auth — an unconditional strip on every 3xx breaks authenticated same-origin redirect flows. Proxy-Authorization is also not origin-scoped: it authenticates the proxy hop, so stripping it while a proxy is in use breaks proxy auth (the 2.x sibling fix explicitly carves this exception out at fix.diff:103-109).

O6_input_shapes: credential headers supplied per call, in mixed case ('Authorization' vs already-lowercased 'authorization'); non-credential headers must survive the strip
Basic auth via options.auth, which is turned into an authorization header at src/HttpClient.ts:416-418 rather than coming from options.headers
Digest auth via options.digestAuth, re-computed after a 401 at src/HttpClient.ts:605-631
client-level defaultArgs.auth / defaultArgs.digestAuth when the call passes no options object at all (client.request(url)), merged in at src/HttpClient.ts:284-293
relative Location (same origin) vs absolute Location on another host, port or scheme (cross origin)
multi-hop chains including A -> B -> A, where a hop that is same-origin with the first URL must still stay stripped
url given as a string or as a legacy url.parse object (normalised at src/HttpClient.ts:265-279)

O7_producer.where: src/HttpClient.ts:191-193 stores ClientOptions.defaultArgs; it is merged into every hop's args at src/HttpClient.ts:284-293 and turned into an authorization header at src/HttpClient.ts:416-418

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a formatRedirectUrl hook that rewrites the resolved Location before the next hop
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the option is still declared and documented for urllib@2 compatibility (src/Request.ts:113, README.md:77) but unimplemented in 4.x, so a maintainer adding it would naturally compute cross-origin from the raw Location and miss the rewritten target

O8b_injection_room.sibling: retry / socketErrorRetry of a request that has already been redirected, re-entering #requestInternal with the caller's original options
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: both retry paths already re-enter with the caller's `options` (and src/HttpClient.ts:776-783 on socket error), so a retry after a stripped hop can re-attach credentials

O8b_injection_room.sibling: response-derived Cookie copied from a 401 Set-Cookie into the following request's headers
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: an existing credential-forwarding line sits right beside the redirect branch and already carries a server-supplied value across a request boundary

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an urllib-owned redirect policy in the fetch transport instead of delegating redirects to undici
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: fetch is a second public transport in the same package sharing the same dispatcher, and urllib already wraps undici calls it does not trust (src/fetch.ts:11)

O9_family: credential / sensitive-data exposure on cross-origin redirect (CWE-200, CWE-201, CWE-522)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Delete or blank the Authorization entry in options.headers inside the redirect branch and keep passing the same options object through, so options.auth / options.digestAuth and client defaultArgs.re-auth re-create the header on the next hop (and the caller's reusable options get mutated).

out_of_scope_notes: 307/308 redirects also replay the request body to the new origin because the redirect branch passes the same args through; the advisory only covers request headers, so this was not pursued.

Pattern A is thin in this tree: the second implementation (fix.diff:17-117, lib/urllib.js) belongs to the 2.x/3.x branch and is absent at the pinned commit, so the only in-tree out-of-scope layer is the ClientOptions.defaultArgs merge (src/HttpClient.ts:191-193, 284-293).

fetch() (src/fetch.ts:224) delegates redirects to undici; whether undici 7.24 strips authorization/cookie/proxy-authorization on a cross-origin redirect was not verified because undici is not vendored in the tree. If it does not, that would be an O8 route.

Whether any existing pinned test asserts credential headers survive a cross-origin redirect was not exhaustively checked; the redirect tests that exist (test/options.followRedirect.test.ts) assert only status/url/requestUrls.
